name: Gofish
headline: Mathematics master's student exploring Agent RSI and Physical AI.
intro: I turn to mathematics for clarity, and to mountains and daily life for perspective.
heroCaption: Give my steps to the wild, and my curiosity to the world.
about: Hi, I'm Gofish. I'm currently pursuing a master's in mathematics at Southern University of Science and Technology, after studying Mathematical Foundation Science at Dalian University of Technology. Mathematics is where I begin to understand problems, and AI keeps bringing me new ones.

What fascinates me most is how agents improve themselves through experience, and how intelligence can truly enter the physical world through perception and action. I hope to find my own research direction between solid mathematical thinking and concrete experiments.
Off screen, I love traveling, badminton, cooking, and movies. To me, studying a problem seriously and cooking a meal seriously are both worth the effort.

research.title: To lick, or not to lick?
research.subtitle: KFC Original Recipe · Reinforcement learning
research.description: When is the best moment to lick your fingers? I want to model grease buildup, cooling chicken and the reward of a lick, then compare licking after every bite, waiting until the end and adaptive policies. An advertising slogan becomes a sequential decision problem.

details.approach: Represent the state with grease, remaining chicken and temperature; choose to eat, lick or wipe. Solve a small model with dynamic programming, then see whether Q-learning approaches its optimal policy.
details.evaluation: Compare reward, time and accumulated discomfort under the same conditions, then vary preferences. Reward only grease actually removed, so endless licking cannot become a shortcut to a high score.

research.title: Is the middle bun a redundant token?
research.subtitle: McDonald’s Big Mac · LLMs & structured ablation
research.description: Is a Big Mac still a Big Mac with one less bun? Borrowing from context compression and ablation studies, I want to separate the middle bun’s contribution by quantity from its role in the stack, and test whether LLMs can predict the changes in taste and stability.

details.approach: Compare the original, middle-bun removal, an equal bread reduction from the outer buns and reordered layers. Ask an LLM to predict performance from ingredient descriptions and cross-section images before tasting.
details.evaluation: Rate flavor similarity, Big Mac identity, structural stability and personal preference separately, then compare them with model predictions. Tasting better and resembling the original are separate objectives.

researchNotes.title: A better answer needs a baseline
researchNotes.body: Accuracy is one part of improvement. Cost, reliability and failure modes belong in the comparison too.

researchNotes.title: An action is a hypothesis
researchNotes.body: The next observation should tell an agent whether to continue, correct course or ask for help.
